author: Tashner, John
title: Dad only spoke to me once about the Pearl attack — family correspondence
notes:
Jay Tashner's eldest son, born 1944, writing in August 2026. The fuller and the better-informed of the two family accounts: the confusion of the morning as his father described it, the rifle issued without ammunition, the days in the oily water, and then the career — aviation squadrons, fighter squadrons early and anti-submarine work later, an electronics technician through the arrival of radio and radar in aircraft, chief petty officer in a couple of years. He also holds the wartime letters to Jay's mother and to his bride, which this project has not seen.

Oral history at second hand, and it is unusually honest about being that. It opens by saying his father spoke to him about the attack exactly once. It says of the battle of Midway "I need to check but I think he was at the battle of Midway as well" — a witness marking the limit of his own knowledge, which is why this pack records Midway as unconfirmed rather than as a fact, and why this is the most useful sentence in either account. Cited for what Jay Tashner said and what his son believed about him; never for a date, a unit, a ship or a position.

Where it differs from his brother's account — on why the commission was refused, and on whether the war was spent on destroyers or with aviation squadrons — both are carried. His two reasons for refusing a commission are given as his father's own; the third, that his father may have been resisting his mother's ambition for him, he offers explicitly as his own suspicion, and it is quoted as a suspicion.

One checkable claim in it is a year out. The addendum on USS Oriskany says the ship "took its first voyage to the med in 1950"; Oriskany was commissioned on 25 September 1950, first went to sea from New York on 6 December 1950, and departed for the Mediterranean on 15 May 1951. The maiden voyage and the Mediterranean cruise are two things a year apart, and the memory has them as one — which is what this rung is for.
